Game Design Document · Draft

Mountain Kingdoms

A mobile strategy game set in the Caucasus mountains: city building, armies and tower defense, where the mountain passes are the strategic chokepoints that every battle revolves around.

CastlesMountain passesPass GuardiansGuardian kitsHeroesTroopsTotem SpiritsMarches & VIPAlliance eventsResearchWorld map
01 · Core building

Four castles, four identities

Every player picks one of four castle types. The choice is not cosmetic: it sets the kingdom's identity, the starting Pass Guardian and the play style. The castle evolves visually from level 1 to 30, from a humble building to a mighty fortress.

🏰 Stone Keep
Stone, steel and gold: the classic, balanced kingdom.
🛖 Tribal Stronghold
Wood, bone and spirit fire: the wild mountain tribes.
❄️ Ice Sanctum
Ice, crystal and magic: the mages of the frozen north.
⚙️ Iron Citadel
Iron, steam and furnace fire: the lords of industry.

02 · What sets us apart

Mountain passes

Unlike typical open-map games, our world map is split by mountain ranges. Moving between regions means going through narrow passes: chokepoints you cannot go around.

  • Control = power: whoever holds a pass controls the flow of resources and armies in the region.
  • Asymmetric defense: a small force can hold off a large army in a narrow pass.
  • Terrain bond for Guardians: Pass Guardians grow dramatically stronger on pass and peak tiles. The pass is their arena.
03 · Signature feature

Pass Guardians

Like the dragons in King of Avalon and the beasts in KINGSHOT, but with a real Caucasian identity. Legendary giant creatures drawn from mountain mythology; each one leads one march and grows stronger in the passes. Every castle type has its own Guardian, and together they form a role triangle that rewards collecting them all.

Vishap Control · Ice Sanctum
A frost dragon-serpent inspired by the real megalithic dragon stones of the Caucasus highlands. Freezes whole formations and paralyzes enemies in the passes.
Paskunji Burst striker · Stone Keep
A giant eagle from the Caucasus peaks (the Prometheus myth). Fast, first to arrive, diving onto the enemy's rear.
Almasty Tank · Tribal Stronghold
The wild mountain creature of Caucasian folklore. Huge bulk, blocks narrow passes and grows stronger as it takes hits.
Tlepsh Golem Attrition · Iron Citadel
A forge golem named after Tlepsh, the smith god of the Nart sagas. Breaks armor and deals damage over time that wins long battles.
🦅 BurstSpeed and pressure on the rear
🐻 TankHolding the line and blocking
⚙️ AttritionArmor break and damage over time
❄️ ControlFreezing and paralysis

Every hero has three such skills: an active one in battle, a passive on the march, and one for the city or the map. Each skill goes up to level 5 with skill books.

Synergy

  • Hero and Guardian of the same culture: +10% to all march stats.
  • Three heroes of the same culture in a march: another +5%.
  • No culture lock: any player can collect and field any hero, just without the synergy bonus.

This creates a choice in every lineup: a "pure" march for the bonus, or a mixed march that better counters the enemy.

Progression and acquisition

  • "Call of the Peak" recruitment: random recruitment, with a guaranteed legendary hero at least once every 50 pulls.
  • Free path: hero shards from events, pass conquests and daily quests.
  • Starting hero: every player gets the epic hero of the culture they chose.

07 · Collection depth

Totem Spirits

The customization layer and the addictive gacha. You collect dozens of small mountain spirits (eagle, bear, ram, ice spirit, fire spirit…), level them up and merge them, then slot them into each Guardian's 3 slots to shape its abilities.

  • Eagle → +march speed · Bear → +HP · Fire spirit → cancels cold resistance
  • Merging spirits → rarer spirits (a free way to gain power over time)
  • Unlocked and deepened at the top VIP rank
08 · Progression and economy

Marches and VIP

A player can send up to 6 marches at once (attack / reinforce / gather). Each Guardian leads one march. You start with one Guardian (matching your castle); later you can own all four.

RankMain perk
VIP 33rd march slot
VIP 64th march slot + faster gathering
VIP 9Buy or earn a second Guardian beyond your castle's
VIP 12✦ Totem Spirit system + marches 5–6 + own all 4 Guardians

Built-in balance: 6 marches but at most 4 Guardians. There is always room for regular troops, so Guardians never take over.

⚠ Monetization note: do not lock all 4 Guardians behind VIP 12 alone. Offer a slow free path too (events, pass conquests, spirit merging), so VIP speeds up progress instead of being the only wall. Payers pay, free players stay and keep the economy alive.
09 · Alliance events

Two rally events, every 48 hours

Our answer to Bear Trap and the portal events. Both are alliance rally events where the goal is maximum damage. They alternate day by day, so there is always something on, and each one resets every 48 hours. The alliance leader picks the start time to suit most members.

EventHow it playsSkill it tests
💀 Pass GiantThe Div comes down to the alliance's pass for 30 minutes. Members send rallies; the alliance's total damage opens shared chests. Beat him fully and he returns one rank higher.Picking the right Guardian: his weakness rotates each cycle, and a matching Guardian hits 1.5× harder.
🌀 Storm PortalA portal opens on a pass. Players start rallies, members join, and the rally marches in. Rewards go by personal damage and by alliance ranking.Timing: the portal breathes between a shield (×0.5) and an open rift (×2), so the leader launches to land in the rift.

Rewards feed the free path we promised in the VIP chapter: Guardian shards, Totem Spirit essence, hero shards and XP books.

10 · Progression

Research tree

Research happens in the Academy. There are four branches, each with five tiers, and each node levels up from 1 to 10. A node needs the one above it, and the Academy's level caps how deep you can go. The fourth branch, Guardian Lore, and the third, Pass Warfare, are unique to our game.

Troop tiers T1–T10

Every troop type has ten tiers. A new tier needs both a castle level and a Military research. Existing troops can be promoted to the new tier for resources, so nothing is wasted, and every few tiers the troops get a visibly better look in their culture's style, just like the castles.

TierCastle levelResearch
T11Available from the start
T2–T44 / 7 / 10Drill I–III
T5–T913 / 16 / 19 / 22 / 26Forged Arms I–V
T1030Legendary Arms
  • One research at a time; VIP 6 adds a second research queue.
  • Alliance help: every member's help button cuts 1% off the remaining time, up to 20 helps.

11 · The world

World map

Mountain ridges split each realm into six valleys around King's Peak. The only ways between valleys are the passes, nine in all: six between neighbouring valleys and three Royal Passes to the peak.

  • No teleporting across ridges. Every march between valleys goes through a pass, so passes are what alliances fight over.
  • Holding a pass gives a toll on foreign marches, vision of everyone who crosses, and the Guardians' terrain bond.
  • A valley belongs to the alliance that holds most of its passes, with a bonus to gathering inside it.
  • King's Peak opens only during the season war through the three Royal Passes. It is the server's endgame.
  • On the map: castles, resource tiles (wood, stone, food, iron), goblin camps, and the event bosses, which spawn right on the passes.
